amendments.new: Louisiana's 2025 reform set a flat 3% rate and a $12,500 single standard deduction, indexed from 2026 under R.S. 47:294(B). PolicyEngine computed $12,835 from published CPI-U, giving the frozen reference of 3% × ($23,006.18 − $12,835) = $305.14. amendments.old: Most models got AGI right ($106,573) but then made one of three mistakes. Some applied pre-TCJA "sunset" law, others left out the OBBBA senior deduction, and others understated itemized deductions. The reference uses the 2026 OBBBA rules: the 10%/12%/22% brackets with breakpoints at $12,400 and $50,400, and the $6,000 senior deduction phased down by 6% of MAGI above $75,000, which leaves $4,105.65. It adds a 20% QBI deduction of $4,872.35 and itemized deductions of $24,787.23. That itemized total includes estimated Virginia income tax of $5,367.30 in SALT and a $2,434.80 Medicare Part B premium in medical expenses. It excludes the $2,000 of OTC costs and applies the 0.5%-of-AGI floor to charity. The result is taxable income of $72,807.33 and tax of $10,729.61. Models that itemized usually counted only real estate tax, or too little state tax, in SALT, and counted OTC costs instead of the Part B premium in medical.
